title: Intro to AppSec
brief: **Your first step.** Before tools or exploits, you need one mental model of how web apps break. This room gives it to you and checks you understood it.
theory:
## How a web app works
Four parts: **client** (browser), **server** (your code), **database**, and services it calls.

A request has a method, path, headers, body. The server reads this input and may pass it to a **sink** (a DB query, a shell, the HTML page, a file).

## The one idea behind almost every web vuln
> Untrusted input reaches a dangerous operation without the right check in between.

- **Source** = where untrusted input enters (URL, form, header, cookie).
- **Sink** = the dangerous operation it reaches.

## The golden rule
**Never trust input from the client** — even if your own app produced it. The attacker controls the whole request. All real checks happen on the server.
worked_example:
A quick look at a request and response:
```
$ curl -s -D - https://example.com -o /dev/null
HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/html
...
```
The status line + headers are the response metadata. Notice there is no
Content-Security-Policy by default — that is a finding you will meet in the
Misconfiguration room.

investigation.intro: Bring up a web app and look at it as a black box over HTTP.
steps:
Start the lab app:
```bash
cd /workspaces/examto/appsec-lab
python3 -m venv .venv 2>/dev/null; . .venv/bin/activate 2>/dev/null; pip install -q -r requirements.txt
python3 run_server.py               # leave this running
```

In the terminal on the right, in a second shell, hit the app:
```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5000/health
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:5000/greet?name=Kiro"
```
Notice the server echoes your input. Ask yourself: what is the **source** here, and what **sink** does it reach? (You will exploit exactly this in the XSS room.)
hints: The source is the 'name' query parameter.
The sink is the HTML page the server builds.
Remember the golden rule for the task below.

capture.task: **The golden rule:** should you TRUST data coming from the client? Answer `true` or `false`.
